statement: You are given two arrays nums1 and nums2, each sorted in ascending order, of lengths m and n.
Return the median of all m + n values taken together. When m + n is odd, the median is the middle value of the combined sorted order; when it is even, it is the average of the two middle values.

The required running time is O(log(m + n)), so the arrays cannot simply be merged. Binary search on how many elements the shorter array contributes to the left half of the combined order: a split is right when every value on the left is at most every value on the right.

examples.explanation: Together the values are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12. There are 10 of them, so the median is the average of the 5th and 6th: (5 + 6) / 2 = 5.5.
The combined order is −6, −4, −1, 1, 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 8. The two middle values are 1 and 3, so the median is 2.0.
The combined order is 1, 2, 3. With an odd count the median is the single middle value, 2.
